feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Germany's Merz vows to press ahead with reforms after historic state election defeat
entry.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has faced a major electoral setback in two state elections, with his center-right party losing ground. The far-right Alternative for Germany party made significant gains.

entry.title: PHOTOS: The precarious life of fisherfolk
entry.summary: In the bustling heart of the southern Indian city of Chennai is a market that never sleeps, where residents from the poorest neighborhoods wage a battle of survival with the sea.

entry.title: Ukraine fires over 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds launched at Moscow
entry.summary: Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.

entry.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis tried to attack its capital
entry.summary: Saudi Arabia said Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile, the first time its capital has been targeted since the escalation in fighting with the Iran-backed rebels.

entry.title: The new lines of southern Lebanon
entry.summary: The U.N. expanded the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon's mandate 20 years ago to include monitoring adherence to a ceasefire in fighting between Israel and Lebanon's Iran-backed Hezbollah — the militant group created in 1982 to counter a second Israeli invasion.

entry.title: France, Poland and European allies warn of escalating Russian 'hybrid' attacks
entry.summary: The leaders of France, Poland, and other leading European nations are alarmed over what they describe as Russian "hybrid" attacks.

entry.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
entry.summary: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.

entry.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
entry.summary: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.

entry.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
entry.summary: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.

entry.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
entry.summary: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.
